document.abstract: The existing methods for measuring display system parameters are decades old. These methods have always assumed a 4:3 aspect ratio for display devices. This has caused problems in the widescreen cinema film application, and resulted in the use of non-standard measurement methods. Electronic displays have now gotten wider as well, which suggests the time has finally come to re-examine the measurement methods used for displays as a whole. This paper examines the requirements for a more complete, more useful, modernized measurement procedure for characterizing wide display performance. It is aimed primarily at the cinema application, both film and electronic-based, but is equally appropriate for other applications of widescreen projectors and other wide displays.

authors.bio: David Richards is a co-founder and principal at Moving image Technologies (MiT). Prior to co-founding MiT, Richards held engineering and management roles at Christie Digital Systems. He serves on several of the SMPTE DC28 committees as well as the F2 Film and P3 Projection Technology committees. He is Past Chair of the SMPTE Hollywood Section, and was Program Chair for the first and second SMPTE Film Conferences held in 1997 and 1998. Richards is the author of several papers and articles for various trade publications.
